title: Security Testing for Customer-Facing Logistics AI Agents
summary: Adversarial testing of tracking chatbots, WhatsApp bots and voice agents for shipment data leakage, tracking-number enumeration, prompt injection and unsafe actions such as unauthorised redirects.

seo.title: Logistics Chatbot and Voice AI Security Testing | VipraTech
seo.description: Red-team testing of logistics chatbots and voice agents for data leakage, tracking enumeration, prompt injection and unauthorised address or COD changes.

problem.intro: Carriers, 3PLs and e-commerce logistics teams are putting LLM-based chat and voice agents in front of customers, riders and shippers. These agents look up shipments, change delivery details, reschedule and sometimes touch COD or refund flows, which makes them attractive targets for fraud and data harvesting.

pain_points.title: Shipment data exposure
pain_points.detail: A poorly guarded agent may reveal consignee names, phone numbers or addresses to anyone who supplies or guesses a tracking number.

pain_points.title: Redirect and parcel fraud
pain_points.detail: Social engineering through the agent can change a delivery address, release a held parcel or reroute a high-value shipment.

pain_points.title: Prompt injection through inputs
pain_points.detail: Instructions hidden in a message, an address field or an uploaded document can steer the agent to ignore rules or reveal its system prompt and tools.

pain_points.title: Voice-specific risks
pain_points.detail: Voice agents face impersonation, switching between Hindi and English to slip past filters, and pressure tactics that text-only testing misses.

solution.overview: We run structured adversarial testing against your chat, WhatsApp and voice agents before launch and after major changes. We map what the agent can see and do, then attack it: tracking-number enumeration, identity bypass, address-change and reroute fraud, COD and refund manipulation, prompt injection through messages and form fields, disclosure of system prompts and tools, and off-topic misuse. Voice agents are tested with multi-turn calls in Hindi, English and Hinglish. Every attempt is logged with transcript or recording, classed as pass, risk or fail, mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications, and paired with a concrete fix.
capabilities: Maps the agent's data access, tools and actions into a threat model
Tests tracking-number enumeration, identity verification bypass and data leakage
Attempts address-change, reroute, COD and refund manipulation through conversation
Runs prompt injection through messages, address fields and uploaded documents
Tests voice agents with multi-turn Hindi, English and Hinglish adversarial scripts
Delivers pass, risk or fail evidence with fixes and a re-runnable regression pack

workflow.title: Scope and threat model
workflow.detail: We agree in-scope agents, environments and rules of engagement, and map data access and actions.

workflow.title: Write attack playbooks
workflow.detail: Playbooks are written for your flows: tracking, reschedule, address change, COD and B2B portals.

workflow.title: Execute tests
workflow.detail: Automated and manual attacks run across chat, WhatsApp and voice, with every attempt recorded.

workflow.title: Classify results
workflow.detail: Each attempt is classed as pass, risk or fail with evidence and mapped to recognised frameworks.

workflow.title: Review with your team
workflow.detail: Findings are walked through with security, product and CX teams, who decide fixes and accepted risks.

workflow.title: Retest and hand over
workflow.detail: Fixes are retested, and a regression pack is handed over for future releases.

human_in_the_loop: Our testers review every automated result before it is reported, and your security, product and CX owners decide which fixes to make and which risks to accept. Testing runs only within the agreed scope and under written authorisation.
integrations: Voice agent numbers or SIP endpoints in test

guardrails: Written authorisation and agreed scope before any test
Synthetic shipments and test accounts only; no real consignee data

Findings shared only with named contacts
Every reported finding reproducible from saved evidence
compliance_notes: Findings are mapped to the OWASP Top 10 for LLM Applications and the NIST AI RMF to support your security governance.
Helps you evidence reasonable security safeguards for personal data under the DPDP Act 2023.

pilot.scope: One customer-facing agent, such as the WhatsApp tracking bot or the delivery status voice agent, tested in staging with synthetic shipments.
deliverables: Findings report with severity and fixes

what_we_measure.how: Successful attacks classed on an agreed severity scale.
Agent tools and actions exercised by at least one attack, out of all mapped actions.
Findings retested and confirmed closed after changes.
Attack playbooks executed per language for voice and chat.

faqs.a: We prefer staging with synthetic shipments. If production testing is required, it runs under written authorisation, with agreed rate limits and test accounts only.

faqs.q: How is this different from a normal penetration test?
faqs.a: A web or API penetration test looks at the application and infrastructure. We focus on how the AI agent can be manipulated through conversation, prompts and tools, and add API checks where the agent's actions depend on them.

faqs.q: Can you test voice agents in Hindi?
faqs.a: Yes. Voice playbooks run as real multi-turn calls in Hindi, English and Hinglish, including code-switching, impersonation and pressure tactics. Recordings are kept as evidence.
After any change to prompts, models, tools or verification rules, and before peak seasons. The regression pack makes retesting a routine release step.
